proposal.blind_spot: All kernels stall on long-scoreboard global-load latency with unsaturated DRAM, but the optimizer cannot tell whether the L1/TEX pipe is the throughput ceiling (needs fewer transactions) or is idle (needs more memory-level parallelism), nor whether loads hit in L2 (hideable latency, exploit reuse) or stream from DRAM (needs locality restructuring or efficient streaming).

rationale.l1tex__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustai: HIGH -> L1/LSU data path is the ceiling: reduce transaction count via 128-bit vectorized loads, coalesced layouts, and hoisting redundant per-element loads into registers. LOW -> pipe is idle and the kernel is pure latency-bound: increase in-flight loads by processing multiple elements per thread, unrolling reductions, and raising occupancy.
rationale.lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct: HIGH -> loads are served from L2: tile so each byte is loaded once, stage reuse in shared memory/registers, and hide moderate L2 latency with unrolling/prefetch. LOW -> traffic streams from DRAM with no captured reuse: restructure for locality (block the reduced dimension, smem staging) or, for single-pass streaming ops, maximize sector efficiency and MLP instead of speculative access-pattern rewrites.

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:It splits on global-load sector utilization (coalescing) together with waves per SM (block-level parallelism relative to occupancy), which are durable hardware regimes, whereas the barrier-stall cut is near-zero and the DRAM cut is not a clean saturation boundary.
